value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized statewide budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025 and remains an active program per SGIP's own statewide announcements (most recently dated 2026-07-23). Administered across PG&E's entire distribution territory, which includes Pacific Grove/Monterey County.
value.eligibility: PG&E, SCE, or SDG&E residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Reused as a utility-level fact already established for other IOU-territory records this session: the CPUC-administered SGIP program applies uniformly across the named utility's entire distribution territory, directly verified via SGIP's own site (selfgenca.com) / the CPUC's own SGIP program page, including a program-status announcement as recent as 2026-07-23 confirming the program remains active.

value.name: Standard plan and checklist of all requirements, published on the City's website, substantially conforming to the California Solar Permitting Guidebook

required_documents.notes: Per Pacific Grove Municipal Code Section 18.45.050(a)-(e): the building department creates a standard plan and checklist substantially conforming to the CA Solar Permitting Guidebook, made available to the public via the city website.

value: Only one inspection may be required and performed by the building department for eligible small residential rooftop solar energy systems
The inspection shall be done in a timely manner and should include consolidated inspections; an inspection will be scheduled within two business days of a request
If a small residential rooftop solar energy system fails inspection, a subsequent inspection is authorized
inspection_steps.notes: Per Pacific Grove Municipal Code Section 18.45.060(h)-(j).

value.notes: Pacific Grove Municipal Code Section 18.45.060(a): the building department 'shall issue a building permit or other nondiscretionary permit within three business days for over-the-counter applications or up to three business days for electronic applications' of receipt of a complete application.

value.program_or_pathway: Expedited small residential rooftop solar permitting (Pacific Grove Municipal Code Chapter 18.45)
other_conditions: System must be installed on a single- or duplex-family dwelling
Solar panel/module array must not exceed the maximum legal building height as defined by the city planning commission
Electronic submittal of required applications/documents is available by email, internet, or fax, and electronic signatures are accepted in lieu of wet signatures

value.notes: Per the City's FY 2025-26 fee schedule.
